### 2026-08-09 (branch `grass-dirt-adjudication`, off `window-adjudication-decomp` b8931249) — THE TOP ORDER-STABLE ITEM WAS A CARVER RE-GRASSING PASS, AND THE STUB WAS ONLY HALF OF IT

**Closed, repaired, gated.** The ranked item was
`grass_block[snowy=false] -> dirt`, 646 against a per-kind vanilla-vs-vanilla
floor of 1, 76% of the order-stable core and 88% of it net of declared gaps.
It is one item, it is a defect, and it is fixed.

Everything below: seed 20260722, centre chunk (64,64), r=16, 1,089 chunks,
bbox `48 48 80 80`, 107,053,056 blocks, full height, `GEN_ORDER=rows`,
**VANILLA FIRST**, eight unmodified references
`oracle-work/gen-wide-20260722-r16-ow-{a..h}`, Threadripper.

#### The delta — the same eight fixed references before and after

```text
  N=8 admissible charge        14,270  ->  13,620      -650
    no longer charged                          650
    NEWLY charged                                0
  N=2 admissible residual (a,b) 20,244  ->  19,594      -650
    99.981090%              ->  99.981697%
  grass_block[snowy=false] -> dirt   646  ->  0
    per-kind twin floor of that pair            1
    `grass_block` kind twin floor               5   (`dirt` 232)
```

Both "before" figures are this branch's parent's published ones and both were
re-derived here before anything was changed: 14,270 by intersecting the eight
`<ref>-vs-ours.pos` position sets, 20,244 by `ci/admissible-residual.py`
itself. So the delta is against a measured baseline, not a quoted one — and
poison control A below closes the last gap in that by re-taking the baseline
in *this* tree at *this* worker count and getting 14,270 with **zero**
positions moved. Nothing new is charged anywhere in the window: the change is
monotone.

Also removed for free, uncharged and not sought: `grass_block -> clay` 3,
`short_grass -> air` 1. That is the 650 against the 646.

**A level is not quotable here and a delta is.** At N=8 this window has no
floor of its own; the brief's 16,932 is an N=6 innocent floor taken against
the N=2 residual. `docs/DETERMINISM.md` §13 is unchanged by any of this.

#### What it was

`WorldCarver#carveBlock` (26.2 bytecode, `server-26.2-unsigned.jar`) re-runs
the surface rule on the block **below** a carved one, once the column has
passed a `grass_block` or `mycelium`:

```text
  reachedSurface.isTrue()
    && chunk.getBlockState(pos.below()).is(Blocks.DIRT)
    -> CarvingContext#topMaterial(biomeGetter, chunk, below,
                                  !carveState.getFluidState().isEmpty())
```

That is why vanilla's cave mouths keep a grass lip and ours kept bare dirt.
`SurfaceSystem#topMaterial` is much cheaper than the surface stage and the
difference matters: it builds a one-shot `SurfaceRules$Context`, compiles the
`RuleSource`, and calls `tryApply(x, y, z)` **once**, with `stoneDepthAbove`
and `stoneDepthBelow` both **hardcoded to 1** — no column walk — and the
biome `Set` argument `null`. The fluid flag has exactly one use:
`waterHeight = y + 1` when the block just carved above holds fluid, else
`Integer.MIN_VALUE`. That single bit is what picks `grass_block` over `dirt`.

**The set reads as a *ring* on the surface and that is the mechanism, not a
coincidence.** The interior of a cave mouth exposes stone, which the `DIRT`
test rejects; only the rim exposes dirt. Chunk (49,70), 73 of the 646:

```text
  1122  .....#.####.....
  1123  ..###.....##....
  1124  ###........#####
  1127  ...##.......###.
  1133  ......#######.##
```

#### TWO DEFECTS, AND THE FIRST ONE HID THE SECOND

`carve_block` armed `hasGrass` with `existing == "minecraft:grass_block"` — a
**state** string compared against a **block** name. Vanilla's
`BlockState#is(Block)` ignores properties, and the overworld surface rule's
own `result_state` in `data/minecraft/worldgen/noise_settings/overworld.json`
carries `"Properties": {"snowy": "false"}`. So the arm could never fire in the
real generator and the `top_material` call site below it was **unreachable**.

That is why `golden_carver_chunk`'s `topMaterial was asked for 0 times` was
green over 82 chunks: it was measuring a dead arm, not measuring a world with
no cave mouths in it. **Rule 7 payout.** Fixing the arm alone changes nothing
(the closure still answered `None`); implementing the closure alone changes
nothing (it is never called). Only both together move a block.

```text
  topMaterial asks over the r=16 window        0  ->  4,897
  topMaterial asks in golden_carver_chunk      0  ->      9
```

#### POISON CONTROLS — two, and both could have failed

**A. Revert the `hasGrass` arm, keep the real closure.** The prediction was
that the closure alone does nothing, because it is never called.

```text
  topMaterial asks             0
  N=8 admissible charge   14,270      (baseline 14,270)
  positions changed vs baseline    0  in either direction
```

Bit-identical to the baseline. So the arm was the whole gate, the old code's
"0 asks" was **structural rather than lucky**, and — because this dump was
taken in *this* tree at *this* worker count — the before figure is not an
artefact of the tree that produced `decomp-ours-r16`. The before/after are
same-tree.

**B. The lazy implementation: `topMaterial` returns
`grass_block[snowy=false]` unconditionally.** This is the fix somebody writes
if they read the ring as "vanilla keeps grass here". The prediction was that
it removes the same 646 and is caught anyway.

```text
  topMaterial asks         5,029
  N=8 admissible charge   13,797      (correct fix 13,620)
  no longer charged          650      the same 650
  NEWLY charged              177      dirt -> grass_block  168
                                      clay -> grass_block    9
```

**So the instrument convicts a wrong material by 177 blocks, and the window
does exercise the choice rather than just the trigger.** The nine `clay` are
worth naming: the surface rule's clay bands answer at some of these positions,
which no "put the grass back" rule could ever produce. Note also that the ask
count is not a fixed property of the terrain — `topMaterial`'s own write feeds
the `DIRT` test one block further down — so 4,897 against 5,029 is expected
and is not a second finding.

#### Coverage, and one thing this window does *not* cover

```text

    of them under a fluid                 632   the flag's only use is
                                                waterHeight = y+1, so this
                                                branch IS exercised

```

`golden_carver_chunk`'s target double answers `top_material` with `None`, so
that gate exercises the **trigger** — `hasGrass`, the `DIRT` test, the DOWN
offset — and never the **material** the surface rule picks. The material is
adjudicated on the r=16 window and nowhere else, and poison control B is what
says the window can actually adjudicate it.

**A miss on the stored biome declines rather than guesses.** The fuzz reaches
one chunk out, so on the outer ring of the *generated* area `id_at` can land
on a container that was never filled; the closure answers `None` there, which
is exactly what the stub did, so a miss can only fail to improve a block and
can never move one the wrong way. It is counted and printed, and it is **29**
over this window — **not** the zero this paragraph said before the counter
existed. The earlier build guessed `BiomeId::default()` at those 29 and its
dump is byte-identical to the declining one, so the two agree here and only

#### Nulls — killed here, do not re-run

* **Not the surface rule.** Around all 646 positions the column y-3..y+4 is
  vanilla's, exactly: 5,168 neighbour slots compared, **3 differ** — and those
  3 are two positions belonging to the separately-charged
  `short_grass -> tall_grass` and `air -> brown_mushroom` items. Only the top

  with vanilla's own column above and below it, and 646/646 have air directly
  above (442 with air for three blocks, 192 with vanilla's own `short_grass`
  standing on our dirt).
* **Not a decorator and not chunk order.** 646/646 order-stable, re-derived
  independently from `~/rp-logs/decomp-orders/`.
* **Not a structure.** None of the 646 is in any of the window's 1,087 piece
  boxes (parent commit b8931249).
* **Not a lake or a shoreline.** The ring shape and the y=62/63 peak read as a
  pond rim and are not one: they are cave-mouth outlines, and the y peak is
  where cave mouths meet the terrain, not where water is.
* **`ci/decorate-order-intersect.sh` was not run and did not need to be** —
  `ci/order-stability.sh` answers the stronger form of the same question and
  had already been run on this set.

**A trap for the next agent who parses `region-differ diff --positions`.** A
`.pos` file is not only positions: it ends with a confusion table and an
`Examples:` block, and an example line has **five whitespace-separated fields**
just as a position line does. `awk 'NF==5'` therefore eats them, and they are
byte-identical strings across reference files, so they survive an intersection
and inflate the count. It cost this turn an N=2 residual of 20,245 against the
published 20,244 — small enough to look like a rounding story and it is not
one. Anchor on the shape of the key:
`$1 ~ /^-?[0-9]+$/ && $2 ~ /^-?[0-9]+$/ && $3 ~ /^-?[0-9]+$/ && $4 ~ /^minecraft:/`.
Every figure in this entry was re-derived with that filter and
`ci/admissible-residual.py` agrees with it to the digit at N=2.

**Closed.** The section below recommended spending this window on its one
adjudicable defect rather than trying to rescue its aggregate. That is done.

in one command, `GD_SEED=12345` for the second window.

**What moved.**

| window | base cef0f06b | with the fix | delta | newly charged |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| seed 20260722 r=16 (N=8) | 2,436 | **1,786** | **-650** | **0** |
| seed 12345 r=16 (N=5) | 7,940 — 99.992583% | **7,704 — 99.992804%** | **-236** | **0** |

`grass_block[snowy=false] -> dirt` goes **646 -> 0**, and the join that clears
its own floor in both directions goes **650 -> 4**. On 20260722 every one of
the nine references improved by *exactly* 650 positions. **20260722 remains
`quotable = false`, disqualifier `below floor`** — 1,786 is still inside its
innocent floor and no percentage may be taken from it. **The seed-12345 arm is
the quotable half**, and its floor did not move: the whole improvement is in
the charge.

**What it was.** `WorldCarver#carveBlock` re-runs the surface rule on the
block below a carved one once the column has passed a grass_block or mycelium
(`is(Blocks.DIRT)` on the block below, then `CarvingContext#topMaterial`), so
vanilla's cave mouths keep a grass lip and ours kept bare dirt. **Two defects,
and the first made the second unreachable:** `carve_block` armed `has_grass`
by comparing a *state* string against a *block* name, which vanilla's
`BlockState#is(Block)` does not, so the arm could never fire — and the closure
below it was separately stubbed to `None`. Either alone hides the other, which
is why the caveat said "stubbed" while `golden_carver_chunk` asserted
`topMaterial was asked for 0 times` and both were green.

**The census named the suspect before any class was opened** (rule 9): the 646
are one block deep in all 646 of their columns, y 50..85 peaking at sea level,
60 of 1,089 chunks, 191 clusters with median size 1, and a chunk-border share
of 11.6% against 12.5% for a uniform scatter. A one-block skin at sea level in
small rings, off the seams — a cave mouth's lip.

monotonically with every reference added with no place to stop, and it

to its N and to its harvest order.*

#### The nether, re-taken too, and still corroboration-only

Eight fresh references (6 `rows`, 2 `rows_rev`), y 0..127, 35,684,352 blocks.
Floor 766,490 against residual 108,479 at N=6 — 7x, and the gap widens with N,
so there is no N at which the r=16 nether becomes quotable. Matching the order
buys **27%** here (108,479 → 79,334) against the overworld's 83%: the overworld
residual was mostly chunk order and the nether's is mostly not.

#### Killed — do not re-run these

* **"The N=6 ladder cannot be re-taken."** It can, and it costs seven minutes.
  Nobody had priced a reference; it is 70 s.
* **Widening the ensemble as the way to control chunk order.** Measured, works
  (2,570 at N=11), and rejected on method — see above. Do not re-open it as a
  way to rescue a level figure.
* **Reading a converged residual as a defect count.** Killed twice now, once in
  the old §4 and once here.
* **`region-differ scan` refusing `--ybox`.** It accepts and ignores it.
* **The idea that a floor is code-dependent.** It is not, at any N, in either
  dimension — measured, not assumed.

#### Instrument defects found by running the instruments

* A missing floor printed as **0**, which reads as "no noise" and is exactly
  how the End's floor came to be published as zero. It prints an em-dash now.
* `ci/floor-ladder.py`'s self-check was hard-coded to the overworld's floor and
  **refused a correct nether run** at 377,949 against 29,560. Keyed on the
  window now, with a loud `!! NO SELF-CHECK` line where none is registered.
* A self-test built from plain `set` literals could not see a
  `set.intersection` type error against the frozensets the real loader returns.
* `ci/order-level-retake.sh` certified two **missing** dump directories as
  proof the order knob had turned, because `diff -rq` on two absent paths also
  reports "they differ". Coverage before comparison.

Not on this window, and not another ensemble. Two candidates, in order:

### 2026-08-10 (branch `chunk-order-residual`, off `window-adjudication-decomp` b8931249) — CLOSED: THE ORDER DEPENDENCE IS SHARED WITH VANILLA, AND VANILLA HAS MORE OF IT

**Closed.** The brief asked whether we are order-dependent where vanilla is
not, and said a well-evidenced *"the dependence is shared and the residual is
noise"* would be a full close. It is shared, and by a wide margin.

Everything below: seed 20260722, centre chunk (64,64), r=16, 1,089 chunks, bbox
`48 48 80 80`, 107,053,056 blocks, full height, VANILLA FIRST, Threadripper.
`docs/DETERMINISM.md` §14 is the argument and ORACLE rule 29 is the rule;
this is the worklist form.

#### The one number

```text
  |innocent vanilla, rows_rev, ∉ V| over the eight rows references   117,628
  |innocent vanilla, rows,     ∉ V| over the same eight                3,804
  |ours, x-major dump,         ∉ V| over the same eight               14,270
  |ours, zx dump,              ∉ V| over the same eight                2,450
```

`rowsrev-a` is unmodified vanilla of the same seed and window differing from
the references in one controlled way: the chunk rows are walked z-descending.
**The instrument charges a vanilla run 117,628 blocks for the wrong chunk
order.** Our whole residual was 14,270.

#### What was actually wrong

`Area::chunks()` walks x outer, z inner (`pipeline.rs:182`).
`ci/gen-vanilla-region.sh GEN_ORDER=rows`, which is how every r=16 reference was
harvested, forceloads one z row at a time, z ascending — which is our `zx`. The
comparison had an uncontrolled variable in it.

Two independent fixes, both measured, take it to about the same place:

```text
  match the dump order to the harvest      14,270 -> 2,450   (zx)
  widen the ensemble to hold both orders   14,270 -> 2,583   (N=10)
```

and the attribution control says which kind of reference did the work: a ninth
**same-order** reference buys 307 blocks, two **order-varied** ones buy 11,687.

#### The falsification, written before the run

If `zx` won because it is the harvest order, then against `rows_rev` references
`zx_zrev` must win and `zx` must lose by about as much. It did:

```text
  vs rows refs (N=2)      zx      6,323  best      zx_zrev  131,111
  vs rows_rev refs (N=2)  zx_zrev 6,025  best      zx       126,053
```

#### Vanilla's own order sensitivity

```text
  rows-a vs rows-i        32,127    same order, different run
  rows-a vs rowsrev-a    146,169    different order
  rows-b vs rowsrev-b    152,538    different order
```

4.6x. **Do not assume vanilla is the stable one.**

#### Killed — do not re-run these

* **"We are order-dependent where vanilla is not."** Dead. Vanilla moves
  146,169 blocks between orders; our whole sweep spans 18,508..210,373 against
  our default, the same magnitude.
* **Region-file boundaries as the geometry.** 12.8% of the moved set and 16.0%
  of the charged part sit on a region-edge chunk against a uniform 11.75%.
* **A stage earlier than decoration.** 0 of 107,053,056 through
  `RUSTMC_THROUGH=carvers` under two orders, 201,818 through `decorated` on the
  same command path. State it honestly though: the knob is only read by the
  decoration traversal, so the carvers arm shows the earlier stages are
  byte-deterministic rather than that the knob was live and inert.
* **Our generator being non-reproducible.** Five of five `diff -rq` identical,
  same tree and across trees.
* **Picking the best order by score.** That is fitting; the harvest order is
  determined a priori and the `rows_rev` arm is what proves it.

#### What is left on this window

`charged under EVERY order` is **853 / 853 / 852 / 852** at N=8/9/10/11 — it
does not move when the ensemble is widened, which is what says it is real. It is
§13's order-stable core and 646 of it is `grass_block[snowy=false] -> dirt`,
which is another agent's item. With order controlled our charge sits **below**
the innocent vanilla floor at every N (sep −2,061 at N=7), so **this window is
finished as an adjudicator above about 2,500 blocks.** That is not a fidelity
claim — a deterministic generator locked to the references' harvest order beats
a vanilla run carrying scheduler jitter.

#### Next item

Not on this window. The single next thing this leaves is mechanical and belongs
to whoever next takes a level claim: **re-take the r=16 headline with the dump
order matched to `HARVEST-ORDER`, or with an ensemble that holds both orders**,
and register it — the currently registered 29,605 / 99.972345% was taken
x-major against a rows-only ensemble and is measuring the order along with
everything else. Deltas taken that way are still exact and still comparable to
each other; the level is the part that moves.

### 2026-08-09 (branch `window-adjudication-decomp`, off `aquifer-fluid-levels` 74a35692) — THE WINDOW IS NOT FINISHED; IT NEVER HAD A FLOOR MEASURED, AND NOW IT HAS EIGHT REFERENCES

**Closed.** The brief asked whether the r=16 window can still adjudicate at a
20,244 admissible residual against a 29,560 twin floor, and said a
well-evidenced *"this window is finished"* would be a full close. The honest
answer is neither yes nor no as posed, because **the two numbers were never
comparable and the comparison is what needed killing.**

Everything below: seed 20260722, centre chunk (64,64), r=16, 1,089 chunks,
bbox `48 48 80 80`, 107,053,056 blocks, full height, `GEN_ORDER=rows`, VANILLA
FIRST, Threadripper, branch tip 74a35692. `docs/DETERMINISM.md` §13 is the
argument; this is the worklist form.

#### First: the brief's own figure, reproduced exactly

```text
  |ours ∉ {a,b}|        20,244    99.981090%
  |a ≠ b|  (twin floor) 29,560
```

Both to the digit. So the tree matches the brief and everything below is about
the instrument, not about a moved baseline.

#### The framing that died

`docs/DETERMINISM.md` §12 said of the admissible construction *"nothing is
excluded … there is no mask, there is no floor"*, and then compared the charge
to **the twin mask's width** anyway — 29,605 against 29,560, "45 blocks of
headroom" — and concluded *"do not use it to adjudicate the next worldgen
change."*

**No mask means no blind spot. It does not mean no noise.** Two references
under-sample what vanilla can put at a position, so part of `|ours ∉ {A,B}|`
is charged to *any* run that is neither A nor B — an unmodified vanilla one
included. Nobody had measured that because it needs a third reference and this
window had two.

#### The measurement: six more references, 70 s each

`gen-wide-20260722-r16-ow-{c,d,e,f,g,h}` — **new directories**, nothing
existing touched, same invocation as the published pair (this file, ~line
10379). The ensemble is now **eight**. Substituting an innocent candidate for
ours:

```text
  |ours ∉ {a,b}|   20,244   99.981090%
  |c    ∉ {a,b}|   16,932   99.984184%   <- THE FLOOR. c is unmodified vanilla.
```

The arithmetic closes exactly both ways, which is what says this is sound and
not merely new:

```text
  29,560 = 13,739 (c matches b not a) + 15,589 (c matches a not b) + 232
  29,560 = 12,864 (we match b not a)  + 16,595 (we match a not b)  + 101
```

Like-for-like the headroom is **3,312 blocks, not 45, and not negative.**

#### The ladder, and why it says the residual is mostly real

`ci/window-resolving-power.py`, every candidate against every N-subset:

```text
  N   ours                                floor (innocent vanilla)              sep
  2   18,073..23,313  (med 20,278, n=28)  10,136..23,999  (med 16,063, n=168) +4,215
  4   14,780..16,724  (med 15,448, n=70)   4,048..13,917  (med  8,375, n=280) +7,073
  7   14,272..14,709  (med 14,414, n=8)    2,471.. 6,626  (med  4,511, n=8)   +9,903
```

**Ours asymptotes; the floor does not.** Ours is flat from N=5 at ~14,400
while the floor is still falling at N=7. Had our residual been noise the two
columns would have converged. Also: the twin floor over the 28 pairs now
available runs **26,547..38,778, median 31,949** — 29,560 was one draw.

#### The answer to "at what resolution", which is two answers

* **LEVEL — needs N ≥ 5.** At N=2 the innocent floor alone spans
  10,136..23,999 and our 20,244 sits *inside* it: pick a luckier pair and a
  vanilla run outscores us. **The unusable span is ~13,900 blocks.** That is
  far worse than §12 feared, and it is the part of its verdict that survives.
* **DELTA — exact at any N, down to one block.** The references are fixed
  files and our generator is deterministic, so the charge is a deterministic
  function of our output; before and after against the *same* reference set
  there is no noise at all. **The beard fix's −9,331 is sound.**

What a delta cannot do alone is generalise, and that has a **positional test,
not a threshold**: let `U` be the union of every pairwise disagreement among
the references — where vanilla is not unanimous. Over eight references
`U` = **82,599 positions, 0.077% of the window**. Intersect your moved
positions with `U`; what falls outside is your result. For our tree today, of
the **14,270** charged at N=8, **13,837 are outside `U`** — eight independent
vanilla runs agree and we differ — against 433 inside.

* **The whole per-kind CLEAR list except `grass_block -> dirt` is order

### 2026-08-09 (branch `blockage-stone-replace`, off main `8e283f57`) — `getRandomFacingStairs` IS TWO DRAWS, NOT ONE; THE PIECE BOX IS 14 -> 0 AND VANILLA'S OWN DRAW TAPE AGREES AT ALL 554 POSITIONS

**The 14 blocks left in the r=16 overworld portal box are closed.** The item
said to build the per-position draw tape before attempting a repair, and that
order was load-bearing twice: the tape named the defect, and it then caught a
stale binary that would have been read as "the fix does nothing".

#### The defect, in one line of bytecode

`BlockAgeProcessor.getRandomFacingStairs` sets **two** properties, not one:

```text
  stairs.defaultBlockState()
      .setValue(StairBlock.FACING, Direction.Plane.HORIZONTAL.getRandomDirection(random))
      .setValue(StairBlock.HALF,   Util.getRandom(Half.values(), random))
```

`getRandomDirection` and `Util.getRandom(T[], RandomSource)` are each one
`array[random.nextInt(array.length)]`, so the method is `nextInt(4)` then
`nextInt(2)` — offsets 11 and 27. We drew only the first. `Half.values()` is
`[TOP, BOTTOM]` from `Half`'s own `$values()`: **ordinal 0 is `top`**, which is
neither the alphabetical nor the intuitive order.

`maybeReplaceFullStoneBlock` calls it once per candidate array, so a qualifying
stone block spends **seven** draws and not five:

```text
  0  nextFloat   the 0.5 gate
  1  nextInt(4)  non-mossy stairs FACING
  2  nextInt(2)  non-mossy stairs HALF     <- we did not draw this
  3  nextInt(4)  mossy stairs FACING
  4  nextInt(2)  mossy stairs HALF         <- nor this
  5  nextFloat   mossiness
  6  nextInt(2)  which entry of the winning pair
```

#### The instrument, built first and at both ends

* **Ours:** `RUSTMC_BLOCK_AGE_TAPE=<path>` — one line per `block_age` call with
  the ordered draws. The recorder wraps the **production** `RandomSource` and
  calls the production `block_age_with`, so it cannot agree with a copy of the
  code instead of the code.
* **Vanilla's:** `ci/block-age-golden.sh` +
  `tools/goldengen/vanilla/BlockAgeGolden.java` run vanilla's OWN
  `BlockAgeProcessor.processBlock` in the JVM with a recording `RandomSource`
  injected through `StructurePlaceSettings.setRandom`. The processor reads
  nothing but the block info and the settings and its random is per position
  (`Mth.getSeed(pos)`), so it needs no world, chunk, generator or server —
  which is what makes the tape **exhaustive over the box rather than sampled**.

Position by position and draw by draw, 554 positions, seed 20260722, vanilla's
own saved `ruined_portal/portal_3` at chunk (48,64), box
[768 42 1032 .. 776 50 1039], mossiness 0.2:

```text
  BEFORE  seed mismatches 0, output mismatches 14
          positions with any draw divergence: 18
          first divergent draw index -> count: {2: 18}
  AFTER   seed mismatches 0, output mismatches  0
          positions with any draw divergence:  0
```

**18 diverge, all at index 2, and only 14 of the 18 produce a wrong block** —
the other four land on the same state from a different stream. That is the
whole argument for counting draws rather than diffing blocks, stated as a
measurement rather than as a principle.

`ci/block-kind-census.sh <ours-region-dir> <label> [kind ...]` set-differences

charged as vanilla-only only when *both* references hold that kind there — and
then cross-tabulates: for every vanilla-only position of kind X, what do we
hold there. A one-for-one substitution is a full row in that table and is

#### THE DEFECT — `stage/fluid.rs::should_spread_liquid` writes past `set()`

`LiquidBlock#shouldSpreadLiquid` ends in
`Level.setBlockAndUpdate(pos, OBSIDIAN)`, and `Level#setBlockAndUpdate` is
`setBlock(pos, state, iconst_3)` — **flag 3, bit 1 is `UPDATE_NEIGHBORS`**.
So placing the obsidian notifies its own six neighbours, and every lava among
them with water above converts in turn. **The conversion cascades through the
whole contiguous lava-under-water sheet from a single flood.**

Ours writes the obsidian straight onto the canvas, bypassing
`notify_neighbours`, under this comment:

> Vanilla's `setBlockAndUpdate` is flag 3 and would notify again, but the
> block placed is not a fluid and the only notification this pass models is
> the lava one, so a second round has nothing to find and cannot cascade.

The second round has exactly one thing to find and it is the lava one: the
**lava neighbours of the newly placed obsidian**. The comment, the code and
the module's scope note all agree, and all three are wrong — the same shape as
`getRandomFacingStairs`, where the code, the comment and the test agreed on
five draws against vanilla's seven.

#### NULLS — do not re-run these

  Killed by the census above. Not co-located, not the same y, not the same
  chunks. Do not spend another turn on the coincidence.
* **"vanilla ticks marked liquid positions through `LiquidBlock#tick` and that
  is the missing path."** Read and refuted in the same turn:
  `LevelChunk#postProcessGeneration` does call `BlockState.tick` on a marked
  `LiquidBlock`, but `LiquidBlock#tick` is **bubble columns only** — it never
  reaches `shouldSpreadLiquid`.
* **The aquifer is not the suspect.** Our `should_schedule_fluid_update`
  already has the water-directly-on-the-global-lava-sea arm
  (`computeSubstance` offsets 619..668), and the y=−54 water sheet and the
  y=−56 lava body are **byte-identical** to both references across the whole
  slab. Only y=−55 differs.
* **"the pass is water-only, so the missing obsidian is the unported
  `LavaFluid`."** It is not, and this is the trap the module's own scope note
  set. The pass declines **5,779** marked lava positions in this window
  (`Stats::skipped_other_fluid`) and every one of those declines is still
  correct: a marked lava source with nothing to spread into writes nothing, so
  ticking it would have produced no obsidian. Porting `LavaFluid` would have
  been a large change that closed none of the 28. Do not reopen it on this
  evidence.

#### THE FIX, AND THE TAPE THAT SCORES IT

`run_neighbour_updates` now drains a worklist the way
`CollectingNeighborUpdater` does, in `NeighborUpdater.UPDATE_ORDER`
`{WEST, EAST, DOWN, UP, NORTH, SOUTH}` rather than `Direction.values()`. The
order cannot change the result and the reason is written down rather than
assumed: this pass never removes water and a conversion never adds any, so a
position's predicate is monotone in time; and a conversion only removes lava,
so it cannot enable another. `a_cascade_converts_the_same_sheet_from_either_end`
is that argument as a test.

**`RUSTMC_FLUID_TAPE=<path>` + `ci/fluid-tape.sh <label>`.** One line per
tick, flow write and conversion. It is scored against a **vanilla reference
rather than a golden**, and the reason it can be: everything this pass writes
is water, obsidian or cobblestone and it is the last thing to touch them
before the region is saved, so a saved obsidian *is* a conversion vanilla
made and a saved lava under water *is* one it did not. No JVM, exhaustive over
the window. Three independent scores, because a conversion count would have
read as healthy on the day the pass converted two blocks of thirty:

```text
  tape        160,686 tick   5,779 skip   1,057 flow   35 convert
  PRECISION   35/35 conversions land where vanilla agrees
  RECALL      0 vanilla obsidian/cobblestone positions we still hold as lava
  FLOODS      0 water writes landed where vanilla has no water
  FLUID TAPE GREEN
```

**35 is not a coincidence with 46.** Vanilla's window holds 46 obsidian, 11 of
them the ruined portal's, and the tape converts exactly the other 35.

#### The instrument, built before the repair: `ci/fill-compare.sh`

Every instrument in this tree compared *finished* worlds, so every item
opened on a census began by guessing a stage. Two of the last three such
guesses were wrong.

`ci/fill-compare.sh <seed> <cx> <cz> [--twice] [--beard]` compares three
worlds at one chunk — vanilla's own private `doFill` over a real `ProtoChunk`
(`NetherRealFillProbe --overworld`), our `RUSTMC_THROUGH=noise` dump, and the
finished reference — and puts every disagreement in exactly one of **FILL**
(ours: density, aquifer or ore vein) or **POST** (the fills agree, a later
stage moved it). The FILL half has no twin floor because `doFill` has no
decoration order; `--twice` checks that rather than asserting it (0 lines).

`ci/surface-chunk-golden.sh --chunk <seed> <cx> <cz> <out>` is the next rung:
one named chunk after `buildSurface` and after the carvers, in the same
`<tag> x y z state` format. `region-differ starts` is the third: the piece
boxes a reference wrote into its own chunk NBT, so a beard can be built from
vanilla's boxes instead of from ours.

**The instrument's own blind spot, found and closed rather than shipped.**
Both fills are beardless — the probe gets no `StructureManager`, and our
`RUSTMC_THROUGH=noise` world has no bearding start because
`worldgen-assembly` gates `village_starts` and `trial_chamber_starts` behind
`through >= Through::Decoration`. So a default GREEN says only "our fill
matches vanilla's where neither is bearded", and on chunk (78,53) it said
GREEN over 217 blocks of missing beard. `--beard` reads the reference's own
pieces and hands them to the probe. Both readings measured, neither predicted:

```text
  ci/fill-compare.sh 20260722 78 53            FILL COMPARE GREEN     0 charged
  ci/fill-compare.sh 20260722 78 53 --beard    FILL COMPARE RED     217 charged
                                                 153 vanilla stone / ours air
                                                  64 vanilla stone / ours lava
```

#### THE DEFECT — the reference box is the union **inflated by 12**

`Beardifier::for_structures_in_chunk` pre-filtered each start on its raw union
box against the chunk's bare 16x16. Vanilla tests
`StructureStart.getBoundingBox()`, and that is not the union:

```text
  StructureStart.getBoundingBox()
    = structure.adjustBoundingBox(pieceContainer.calculateBoundingBox())
  Structure.adjustBoundingBox(box)
    = terrainAdaptation == NONE ? box : box.inflatedBy(12)
```

Twelve is `BEARD_KERNEL_RADIUS`, and the inflation exists exactly so that a
chunk holding **none of a structure's blocks** but lying inside its beard
still gets a reference. So every start that stopped short of a chunk was
dropped before the per-piece `isCloseToChunk(pos, 12)` filter could see it,
and that chunk was silently beardless — in the only ring where a beard is
visible and the structure is not.

Chunk (78,53): the `trial_chambers` start at chunk (75,55) has union
`[1144,-42,800 .. 1247,5,881]`, read out of the reference's own NBT and
identical to ours. Its max x is **1247** and the chunk's min x is **1248**.
One block.

**The doc comment, the code and the test all agreed and all three were
wrong** — the `getRandomFacingStairs` shape again. The test was called
`a_start_whose_union_box_misses_the_chunk_beards_nothing` and asserted the
defect as behaviour. With the inflation restored the pre-filter is *provably*
redundant against the per-piece filter (every piece box lies inside the
union); it is kept because vanilla keeps it, and the proof is in the doc in
place of the claim it replaces.

#### Why (A) and (B) were one item after all — which the brief said to test, not assume

The brief said "do not re-assume they are one item with each other — test it".
They are, and not for the reason a grouping would have guessed. The beard fix
was made for the lava and the magma closed with it, +10 in the same run:
`UnderwaterMagmaFeature.isValidPlacement` refuses a position any of whose
horizontal neighbours is `isVisibleFromOutside`, and the neighbours were air
in our world only because the beard that fills them was missing. A *density*
term at the noise stage was gating a *feature* four stages later.

Measured, chunk (78,53), r=4, `RUSTMC_WORKERS=1`:

```text
  chunks with a beard   33 -> 41
  lava in the chunk     64 -> 0
```

* **The aquifer is not either item.** Centres, spread level, fluid type,
  surface level and pressure all verified against vanilla — five methods read

* **"the fill is beardless in every dimension" and "a new window is needed to
  see the beard at all".** Both were in `chunk_gen.rs` as fact; both are
  false, and the second was false when written. The published r=16 window has
  three `trial_chambers` starts and 692 `encapsulate` pieces.
* **The datapack grep is still not a bearding test.** `grep -rl beardifier`
  over `generated-data` matches 0 files and `NoiseRouterData` names it 0

So vanilla's fill, surface and carvers all leave air and only decoration puts

#### The instrument, built before any source was opened: `ci/block-kind-census.sh`

The brief said one command decides whether the obsidian, magma and lava
deltas are one item or three, and there was no such command. `region-differ
census` counts and `region-differ diff` lists mismatched positions; neither
answers *"for this one block kind, which positions does vanilla have that we
do not"*, and a count delta cannot tell a substitution from a coincidence.

`ci/block-kind-census.sh <ours-region-dir> <label> [kind ...]` set-differences
the **positions** of each kind, **twin-checked per position** — a position is
charged as vanilla-only only when *both* references hold that kind there — and
then cross-tabulates: for every vanilla-only position of kind X, what do we
hold there. A one-for-one substitution is a full row in that table and is
invisible in a count.

#### THE ANSWER: NOT CO-LOCATED. Three items, not one.

```text
kind                  vanA      vanB      ours    A-only ours-only twinfloor
obsidian                46        46        20        28         2         0
magma_block           1729      1714      1704        10         0        15
lava                 44643     44643     44711        26        94         0
water              2454673   2454500   2454379      2986      2684      7145
cobblestone           2317      2317      2317         0         0         0
stone              8800982   8801093   8798757      2602       289      1113
```

* **obsidian −26** is the y=−55 interface and nothing else. All 28 charged
  positions are at **y = −55**, in chunks (64,74) ×23, (64,73) ×4, (61,71) ×1.
  Of the 28 we hold **lava at 24 and water at 4**. Twin floor **0**.
* **magma_block −25 is a DIFFERENT item, and 15 of the 25 are not real.** The
  twin floor on that kind is 15; the charged set is **10 positions, all in
  chunk (52,74), at y = −8, −7, −6**. That is an ocean-floor y band forty-odd
  blocks above the interface and nowhere near it. Named below as its own item.
* **lava +68 is mostly a THIRD item.** Of 94 ours-only lava, only **24** are
  the obsidian interface; **69** are in chunks (78,53) and (78,54) at
  **y = −18..−21**, and the 26 vanilla-only lava are elsewhere again
  (y = −21..−30, chunks (61,74), (61,75), (67,74)). Named below.
* water and stone are dominated by their own twin floors (7,145 and 1,113) and

**So the brief's suspicion was right to be a suspicion: right size, right

#### The obsidian: we HAVE the mechanism, and it stops after one step

Of our 20 obsidian, **11 are the ruined portal** at chunk (48,64) y 44..49 and
match vanilla exactly; 9 are at the interface. Vanilla's 46 is the same 11
plus **35**. So this is not a missing feature, it is a mechanism that halts.

The slab at y = −56..−54, `x` 1035..1038, rendered three ways (A / B / ours):

```text
x=1036  y=-54  A/B/O  ...WWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWW...      water sheet, identical
        y=-55  A/B    ....OOOOOOOOOOOOOO.....      vanilla: all obsidian
        y=-55  O      ....OWOLLLLLLLLLLL.....      ours: one flood, two converts
        y=-56  A/B/O  ......LLLLLLLL.........      lava below, identical
```

Vanilla floods **exactly one** block of water down into the lava sheet — at
(1035,−55,1180), which our dump reproduces — and the whole rest of the sheet
becomes obsidian. We flood three more (1035,−55,1182), (1036,−55,1181),
(1037,−55,1182) and convert only each flood's immediate neighbours.

#### THE DEFECT — `stage/fluid.rs::should_spread_liquid` writes past `set()`

`LiquidBlock#shouldSpreadLiquid` ends in
`Level.setBlockAndUpdate(pos, OBSIDIAN)`, and `Level#setBlockAndUpdate` is
`setBlock(pos, state, iconst_3)` — **flag 3, bit 1 is `UPDATE_NEIGHBORS`**.
So placing the obsidian notifies its own six neighbours, and every lava among
them with water above converts in turn. **The conversion cascades through the
whole contiguous lava-under-water sheet from a single flood.**

Ours writes the obsidian straight onto the canvas, bypassing
`notify_neighbours`, under this comment:

> Vanilla's `setBlockAndUpdate` is flag 3 and would notify again, but the
> block placed is not a fluid and the only notification this pass models is
> the lava one, so a second round has nothing to find and cannot cascade.

The second round has exactly one thing to find and it is the lava one: the
**lava neighbours of the newly placed obsidian**. The comment, the code and
the module's scope note all agree, and all three are wrong — the same shape as
`getRandomFacingStairs`, where the code, the comment and the test agreed on
five draws against vanilla's seven.

#### NULLS — do not re-run these

* **"the magma −25 and lava +68 are the same interface as the obsidian."**
  Killed by the census above. Not co-located, not the same y, not the same
  chunks. Do not spend another turn on the coincidence.
* **"vanilla ticks marked liquid positions through `LiquidBlock#tick` and that
  is the missing path."** Read and refuted in the same turn:
  `LevelChunk#postProcessGeneration` does call `BlockState.tick` on a marked
  `LiquidBlock`, but `LiquidBlock#tick` is **bubble columns only** — it never
  reaches `shouldSpreadLiquid`.
* **The aquifer is not the suspect.** Our `should_schedule_fluid_update`
  already has the water-directly-on-the-global-lava-sea arm
  (`computeSubstance` offsets 619..668), and the y=−54 water sheet and the
  y=−56 lava body are **byte-identical** to both references across the whole
  slab. Only y=−55 differs.
* **"the pass is water-only, so the missing obsidian is the unported
  `LavaFluid`."** It is not, and this is the trap the module's own scope note
  set. The pass declines **5,779** marked lava positions in this window
  (`Stats::skipped_other_fluid`) and every one of those declines is still
  correct: a marked lava source with nothing to spread into writes nothing, so
  ticking it would have produced no obsidian. Porting `LavaFluid` would have
  been a large change that closed none of the 28. Do not reopen it on this
  evidence.

#### THE FIX, AND THE TAPE THAT SCORES IT

`run_neighbour_updates` now drains a worklist the way
`CollectingNeighborUpdater` does, in `NeighborUpdater.UPDATE_ORDER`
`{WEST, EAST, DOWN, UP, NORTH, SOUTH}` rather than `Direction.values()`. The
order cannot change the result and the reason is written down rather than
assumed: this pass never removes water and a conversion never adds any, so a
position's predicate is monotone in time; and a conversion only removes lava,
so it cannot enable another. `a_cascade_converts_the_same_sheet_from_either_end`
is that argument as a test.

**`RUSTMC_FLUID_TAPE=<path>` + `ci/fluid-tape.sh <label>`.** One line per
tick, flow write and conversion. It is scored against a **vanilla reference
rather than a golden**, and the reason it can be: everything this pass writes
is water, obsidian or cobblestone and it is the last thing to touch them
before the region is saved, so a saved obsidian *is* a conversion vanilla
made and a saved lava under water *is* one it did not. No JVM, exhaustive over
the window. Three independent scores, because a conversion count would have
read as healthy on the day the pass converted two blocks of thirty:

```text
  tape        160,686 tick   5,779 skip   1,057 flow   35 convert
  PRECISION   35/35 conversions land where vanilla agrees
  RECALL      0 vanilla obsidian/cobblestone positions we still hold as lava
  FLOODS      0 water writes landed where vanilla has no water
  FLUID TAPE GREEN
```

**35 is not a coincidence with 46.** Vanilla's window holds 46 obsidian, 11 of
them the ruined portal's, and the tape converts exactly the other 35.

**(A) `magma_block`, 10 blocks, chunk (52,74), y = −8, −7, −6.** Vanilla holds
`magma_block`, we hold **`deepslate`** at all ten. The count delta is −25 and
**15 of that is the twin floor on that kind** — quote 10, never 25. Ten blocks
in one chunk in a three-block y band is a feature that did not run, not a
terrain disagreement; `UnderwaterMagmaFeature` and `BasaltColumnsFeature` are
the only two levelgen classes in the jar that mention `MAGMA_BLOCK` and the
second is the nether's. **Closes when** the window `magma_block` census reads
1,729 with its twin floor quoted beside it.

**(B) the lava aquifer's level, 94 blocks in two opposite directions.** After

```text
  70 ours-only lava   vanilla holds DEEPSLATE
                      69 of them chunks (78,53) and (78,54), y -18..-21
  24 vanilla-only lava  we hold AIR
                      y -21..-30, chunks (61,74) (61,75) (67,74) (62,75)
```

Both directions are an aquifer **fluid level or barrier**, not a fluid flow:

### 2026-08-09 (branch `worldgen-portal-apron`, off main `cd521254`) — THE APRON WAS ONE MISSING `nextLong`; THE DRAW COUNTER FOUND IT, AND A SECOND PASS NOBODY HAD PORTED FINISHED IT

**The window netherrack census is vanilla's 406 exactly, from 464.** The item
was named as "stream offset, not geometry" and told to build a draw counter
first. Both halves held.

#### The instrument: `worldgen-dump ruined-portal-apron <seed> <ref> [blocks]`

The `mineshaft-ceiling` shape, for `spreadNetherrack`. That pass reads nothing
it has not already written and everything it writes is netherrack or magma, so
the saved region **is** a printout of its draws:

* the apron's radius is one `nextInt(max(1, 8 - avgSpan/2))`, and every
  position within Manhattan `13 - offset` spends a `nextDouble` while
  everything further out is skipped **without drawing** — so a candidate
  offset predicts which draws happen;
* `canBlockBeReplacedByNetherrackOrMagma` refuses air, obsidian, lava and
  `#features_cannot_replace`, and **both** blocks the pass writes are
  replaceable — so a saved block answers the predicate the pass asked, whether
  or not the pass wrote there;
* `placeNetherrackOrMagma` spends a `nextFloat` against 0.07 on a warm portal,
  so the netherrack/magma **spelling** of every apron block is that draw;
* `addNetherrackDripColumn` runs `i > 0 && nextFloat() < 0.5` and writes
  unconditionally, so each column's **depth** is a unary printout of a run.

Slide the stream against the blocks and exactly one entry point survives.
Seed 20260722, chunk (48,64), against `gen-wide-20260722-r16-ow-a`:

```text
  k=0   offset=2    252 wrong of 1082 scored
  k=1   offset=3      0 wrong of 1014 scored   <-- exact
  k=2   offset=3    139 wrong of 1020 scored
  ...  every k in 0..=16 except 1 scores 138-431 wrong
```

**Vanilla enters `spreadNetherrack` at draw 1. Main entered at draw 0 and drew
offset 2 against vanilla's 3** — one ring too wide, which is precisely
"netherrack present where vanilla has none and absent where it has some".

It refuses rather than guesses: a surface portal's apron sits on
`WORLD_SURFACE_WG`, which vanilla does not save, and a buried one is refused
if the saved surface comes within 8 of the box floor.

#### Defect 1 — `placeInWorld`'s `LootTableSeed` draw

`StructureTemplate.placeInWorld` spends **one `nextLong` per placed
`RandomizableContainer`**, off the **piece's** stream, writing it into the
block entity's `LootTableSeed`. It is the only call in the entire template
placement that touches that stream — every processor seeds itself per position
from `Mth.getSeed(pos)`, which is why the in-box blocks were already nearly
right while the apron was not. Every ruined-portal template holds exactly one
chest, and vanilla's own chunk (48,64) saves it at (774,45,1035).

**The seed is loot, and no block diff compares loot, so the draw looked free.**
`place_piece` now takes `Option<&mut dyn RandomSource>`; the portal passes its
stream, the four other callers pass `None` with a note (see the debt below).

#### Defect 2 — `TemplateStructurePiece.postProcess`'s second pass

After `placeInWorld` it walks `filterBlocks(.., Blocks.JIGSAW)` and overwrites
every jigsaw block with its own `final_state` (`getStringOr("final_state",
"minecraft:air")`, then `BlockStateParser.parseForBlock`). A ruined portal's
chain has **no** `JigsawReplacementProcessor`, so it really does write a jigsaw
block and really does rub it out again — before `spreadNetherrack` reads the
world.

`portal_3` has one, at template-local (3,0,4), which under FRONT_BACK + CCW90
about pivot (4,4) from `TP=768,42,1024` lands at **(772,42,1035)** — on the box
floor, inside the apron's inner disk. Vanilla leaves air there and the apron
will not build over air. We left the jigsaw block, which *is* replaceable, so
we spent a `nextFloat` and a whole drip column of draws vanilla never spent and
every later position in the walk was off by that many. **One block, six wrong
apron columns behind it.**

destroyed pair's figures do not apply to any number here.** Before = main

```text
  per-piece attribution, margin 16      361             72           18
```

#### WHAT THE COUNTER SAYS ABOUT US, AND WHY IT NEEDED THE BLOCK DIFF TOO

Pointed at our own regions with vanilla's piece list, the counter recovers


**A per-world replay is self-consistent whichever world it reads**, so the
jigsaw block was invisible to it and only the cross-world block diff found
that one. Both instruments were needed and neither would have done alone. Say

### 2026-08-09 (branch `structures-ruined-portal-blocks`, rebased onto main `51fa7c62`) — THE BIOME TAG WAS A CONVENTION AND THE STUB WAS THE WRONG POINT; 554 -> 27 PER PIECE, WINDOW -498, END UNCHANGED

#### 1. `has_structure/{name}` is a convention vanilla does not keep

T0 was red on this branch:

```text
generate::tests::the_full_pipeline_decorates
.../tags/worldgen/biome/has_structure/ruined_portal.json: No such file or directory
```

`ruined_portal_starts` and `shipwreck_starts` both derived a biome-tag name
from the structure's id. Censused over the extract — 34 structures, **all 34
declare `biomes` as a `#` tag string and none uses a list**, and **five of the
34 name a tag the convention does not build**:

```text
  fortress        -> #minecraft:has_structure/nether_fortress
  jungle_pyramid  -> #minecraft:has_structure/jungle_temple
  mansion         -> #minecraft:has_structure/woodland_mansion
  monument        -> #minecraft:has_structure/ocean_monument
  ruined_portal   -> #minecraft:has_structure/ruined_portal_standard
```

`ruined_portal` is the fatal one rather than merely the wrong one: vanilla
ships seven ruined-portal biome tags and none of them is
`has_structure/ruined_portal`, so the derived name does not resolve to the
wrong set — it does not resolve at all.

`facts::resolve_structure_biomes` reads the field instead, decoding it the way
`HolderSetCodec.create` does — `Codec.either(TagKey.hashedCodec,
homogenousList(element, …))` with `homogenousList` wrapped in
`ExtraCodecs.compactListCodec`. Three shapes: a `#` string is a tag (the `#` is
the *only* thing that makes one, and `resolve_biome_tag` already strips it, so
the raw value goes in unmodified); a bare string is `compactListCodec`'s
one-element form and is a single biome, never a tag; a list is elements, and a
`#` inside one is an error in vanilla (`Identifier` has no `#`) and an error
here. **Both element branches are dead against this extract** and exist so an
unfamiliar shape refuses instead of being misread. Absent field, non-string
entry, tag-in-list and an **empty resolution** all refuse — the last one
because an empty set reads as "no biome qualifies", places nothing, and is
indistinguishable from a correct refusal.

**MAIN'S CALL SITE WAS RIGHT AND WAS MOVED ANYWAY.** The instance already on
main is `shipwreck_starts`. `shipwreck.json` declares
`#minecraft:has_structure/shipwreck` and `shipwreck_beached.json` declares
`…/shipwreck_beached`, so the derived name was correct for both and the read
field resolves to the identical set —
`golden_biome_tags::mains_derived_name_was_right_for_shipwreck` pins that, and
fails if either moves. What changes there is only that the next structure read
through that loop is not relying on a convention 5 of 34 structures break.

#### 2. THE STUB IS THE CHUNK ORIGIN, NOT THE BOX CENTRE — the real defect

With the tag fixed the portal placed, and the pre-registered `554 -> 0` came
back **554 -> 553 with the window 991 blocks WORSE**. It was placed 4 east and
12 south: 531 of our 552 netherrack landed in chunk (48,**65**) and 5 in
(48,64).

`RuinedPortalStructure.findGenerationPoint`, 26.2 bytecode. The box centre is
computed at offset 343 (`BoundingBox.getCenter`) and spent on exactly one
thing, `getBaseHeight(centre.x, centre.z, …)` at 350..377. The stub returned at
409..428 is built from `blockpos14` = `ctx.chunkPos().getWorldPosition()`:

```java
new BlockPos(blockpos14.getX(), i1, blockpos14.getZ())
```

and that same `BlockPos` is the piece's `templatePosition` (offset 100), the
position `isCold` samples at (11..52), and the position
`findValidGenerationPoint` filters the biome on. The port used the centre for
all three.

**Vanilla's own saved `Children[]` said so and nothing was reading it.** Seed
20260722 chunk (48,64) saves `TPX/TPY/TPZ = 768,42,1024` — the chunk origin —
with box `[768 42 1032 .. 776 50 1039]`, whose centre is (772,·,1036).

`the_four_saved_portals_reproduce_field_for_field` gates the *plan* — template,
rotation, mirror, vertical placement, air pocket — and every one of those was
already right. **The position was the one saved field with no gate on it**, and
a block diff cannot localise it: a displaced structure reads as "the blocks are
wrong" and says nothing about why.

So the gate landed with the fix: `worldgen-dump ruined-portal-starts <seed>
<radius> [cx] [cz]` prints OUR starts in the format
`jigsaw-starts <ref> ruined_portal` prints VANILLA's saved ones, with no
generated world — the `nether-fossil-starts` shape. It now reads:

```text
VANILLA  portal_3                         TP=768,42,1024
```

becomes.

`RUSTMC_WORKERS=1`, VANILLA FIRST, twin-masked N=2 against
`gen-wide-20260722-r16-ow-a`/`-b`. Threadripper, 1 gameplay corpus harness
live (`rustmc-pluginhook`) — worldgen dumps are a different class:**

```text

  blocks (denominator)      107,017,525  107,017,525          =
  exactness                  99.972001%  99.972035%

```

**-37 was the pre-registered prediction and -37 is the outcome**: 19 from
`final_state` and 18 from `CrossCollisionBlock.rotate`, the two amounts
structures-trial measured per piece box. The denominator reproduces the
published baseline to the digit, which is why the -37 is believable.

**THE FLOOR NOW EXCEEDS THE RESIDUAL — 35,531 against 29,927 — and that is
the caveat that outranks the percentage.** Rule 6 makes a window whose floor
is larger than its disagreement **corroboration only, never a headline**. The
trial-chamber entry below already warned this was coming ("the overworld's
own floor is now 83% of its residual; this window is nearly out of resolving
power"); with the villages placed and these two fixes it has crossed over. So
**99.972035% is not quotable as an exactness claim** and neither is 29,927 as
a defect count.

**The -37 delta survives that, and the distinction is the point.** The floor
bounds what an *absolute* residual on this window can mean; the delta was
taken against the same reference, the same mask and the same denominator,
and both halves of it were attributed per piece box before the change. A
mask that hides 35,531 positions equally in both runs cannot manufacture a
37-block move in the direction predicted. What this window can no longer do
is tell you what the *remaining* 29,927 are — for that the next measurement
needs a sharper instrument, not this one again.

### What was ported

**1. `ruined_portal`'s entire start, gated with no JVM and no world.** A
ruined portal saves its whole random outcome into `Children[]` — `Template`,
`Rotation`, `Mirror`, `VerticalPlacement`, `TPX/TPY/TPZ` and a `Properties`
compound with all six derived properties. That is the `end_city` `GD` shape
again: one NBT read pins the draw sequence. **Four distinct portals mined out
of references already on the box** (nine saved pieces; the twins agree), and
the port reproduced all four field for field on the first run:

```text
  20260722 (48,64)  portal_3   CCW90  FRONT_BACK  underground      4 refs agree
  20260722 (43,88)  portal_9   CW180  FRONT_BACK  underground      2 refs
  20260722 (92,81)  portal_8   NONE   NONE        on_land_surface  2 refs
  31415926 (49,46)  portal_10  CCW90  FRONT_BACK  on_ocean_floor   1 ref
                    (`ruined_portal_ocean`)
```

**The trap, and why four cases rather than one:** `sample()` short-circuits
at probability 0.0 and 1.0 and **draws nothing**. The underground setup is
1.0, `on_land_surface` is 0.5, the ocean structure is 0.0. So (48,64) spends
no draw on its air pocket and (92,81) spends one — a port that always draws
is right for the second and one place late for the first, which reads
downstream as "the template array is wrong".
`getRandomWithinInterval` returns **max**, not min, on an empty interval, and
also draws nothing.

**2. `final_state` resolves through `parseForBlock`** — 19 blocks. The code
wrote the string verbatim while its own comment named the function it did not
call. Vanilla starts from `defaultBlockState()` and applies only the named
properties, so `minecraft:grass_block` is really `grass_block[snowy=false]`.
Plumbed as `BlockFacts::default_state` -> `Decoration` -> all four
`PieceWorld` impls.

**3. `CrossCollisionBlock.rotate`** — 18 blocks, 9 `glass_pane` and 9
`acacia_fence`. AGENT-BRIEF had listed this as known-open. The four booleans
permute **together**; the new `north` is the old `west`. **The scope was
derived, not guessed, and that is the part worth keeping:** twelve block
types in 26.2 carry boolean `north/east/south/west` and only **four** are
`CrossCollisionBlock` (39 blocks, from `definition.type` in
`generated/reports/blocks.json`). The other eight are `huge_mushroom`,
`chorus_plant`, `fire`, `glow_lichen`, `multiface`, `sculk_vein`, `tripwire`
and `vine` — `VineBlock` and `MultifaceBlock` have their own `rotate` and
`ChorusPlantBlock` has none. A "has the four booleans" predicate would have
silently corrupted every one of them; the golden test gates the **negative**
half against the extract as well as the positive one.

**The one that got through is a real hole, not an equivalence, and the
difference matters.** `<=` against `<` in the weighted setup pick parts from
vanilla only when the running remainder lands on **exactly** 0.0 — with two
0.5 weights that needs `nextFloat()` to return exactly 0.5. No seed in the
four-portal corpus does, so no test can separate them on this data, and a
`<=` port would be silently wrong on the seed that eventually does. It is
left as `<`, which is what the bytecode says, and named here rather than
closed with a test that would only assert the arithmetic back at itself.

**THE INSTRUMENT FAILED FIRST, AND IN A NEW WAY.** The sweep's first run was
killed mid-run and **left injection 9 sitting in the source on the box** —
`opaque == 3` turned to `opaque == 2`. Two things hid it:

* **`rsync -az` did not restore it.** The injection is one character, so the
  file's size is unchanged, and the sweep's own `os.utime` had set a newer
  mtime. rsync's quick check is size plus mtime. **A same-length edit is
  exactly the shape of an injection, so the inner-loop sync in AGENT-BRIEF
  cannot be relied on to undo one** — restore by explicit copy and verify by
  md5 on both sides.
* the python buffered stdout into a redirect, so the log was zero bytes and
  a sweep that had died eight minutes earlier looked like one still running.

Both closed: `restore_all()` now runs from a `finally` and from
SIGTERM/SIGINT and says which files it had to put back; output is
line-buffered. No measurement here is contaminated — T0, the r=16 run and
both End runs all completed *before* the sweep launched, and the censuses

### 2026-08-06 — THE TWO SAVANNA VILLAGES ARE PLACED; r=16 OVERWORLD 37,471 -> 24,402

Branch `village-savanna`, off `main` @ d3b74cc. The section below this one is
the previous turn's (trial chambers) and is still live — it is not superseded,
only preceded.

**How much jigsaw machinery was new: none of it.** The tree already had
`jigsaw::add_pieces`, `template_pool`, `pool_alias`, `processor`, `place`
(with `SinglePoolElement`/`LegacySinglePoolElement` settings), `template`,
`writer`, `pieces` and `placement`, and `village_starts` already rolled the
five-entry `villages` set with `weighted_attempt_order` and filtered by biome
after assembly. **Nothing about villages needed porting.** The whole defect
was one clamp.

**The defect.** `village_starts` took its height through a closure returning
`None` outside the square being generated, and skipped any village whose walk
asked outside it. r=16 at centre (64,64) generates chunks 48..80; both
`village_savanna` starts, (46,77) and (81,77), begin outside it.

**There is no vanilla counterpart to the clamp.** `ChunkGenerator` offsets
0..11: `getFirstFreeHeight` is `getBaseHeight` and nothing else, and
`getFirstOccupiedHeight` is the same call with `iconst_1 isub` after it (which
is where the mineshaft's `- 1` comes from). `getBaseHeight` on a
`NoiseBasedChunkGenerator` is `iterateNoiseColumn` — one beardless column, no
chunk — which is exactly why vanilla can lay structures out at
STRUCTURE_STARTS before a neighbour exists. The clamp also made our output a
function of the window size, which vanilla's is not.

**Measured.** Seed 20260722, centre (64,64), r=16, `RUSTMC_WORKERS=1`,
vanilla FIRST, six independent unmodified-vanilla references. The instrument
reproduced the published baseline to the digit before it was believed about
anything new (floor 35,531 / 53,390 / 60,680 / 67,588 / 73,820; main's
residual 43,041 / 38,706 / 38,007 / 37,901 / 37,471):

```text
                             main      this    change
  residual N=6             37,471    24,402   -13,069  -34.9%
  residual N=2             43,041    29,964
  both village boxes       13,309       720   -12,589  -94.6%
  outside every box        12,979    12,545      -434
  three trial chambers     10,274    10,228       -46
  VISIBLE residual y>=62   11,247     1,087   -10,160  -90.3%
```

Pre-registered before measuring: point estimate 23,500, range 21,500–26,500.
**Outcome 24,402 — inside the range, 902 above the point estimate.** The one
line that missed: I predicted 500–3,000 blocks off `outside every structure
box` from two new `beard_thin` starts and it was **434**.

**The walk is gated piece for piece** against vanilla's own saved
`Children[]`, no JVM and no generated world:

```text
  worldgen-dump village-oracle 20260722 oracle-work/van-village-c4576 7 45 76
  worldgen-dump village-oracle 20260722 oracle-work/van-village-c8076 7 80 76
      (46,77)  1/1 starts  98/98 pieces        (81,77)  1/1 starts  73/73
```

element **type**, element id (feature ids included), rotation, position,
ground level delta and box. Golden vectors are committed at
`crates/rustmc-worldgen/golden/village_savanna_20260722_c{4677,8177}.json`.

**A gate defect found by building the gate.** The first run scored 84/98 and
65/73, and every differing row was identical in rotation, position, gld and

**A published figure was refuted: the End's noise floor is NOT zero.** That was
one pair agreeing by luck. Across six references it is 252 — pairwise 0, 46,
81, 125, 171, 206. `PARITY.md` §2/§6 and the wide-window doc are corrected in
place; the wrong text is kept because it was published.

**Vanilla's non-determinism is concurrency, proved by gradient** on the nether
probe window (chunks 70..80², y 0..127, two harvests per row):
`rows`+23 workers 170,797 → `perchunk`+1 worker 100,130 → +`taskset -c 0`
**15,007**. Content intact (basalt 1,774,424 vs 1,773,600), so it is order
noise removed, not generation lost. The families that move are
basalt↔blackstone↔netherrack — the `count_on_every_layer` basalt-deltas
signature, which reads a neighbour's ground y.

**KILLED — do not re-run: determinism by configuration.** `max.bg.threads` is
the ONLY worldgen-relevant system property in the jar (every
`System.getProperty` constant in the server was enumerated). Pool width,
`GEN_ORDER=perchunk`, `taskset`, `-XX:ActiveProcessorCount=1`, `+UseSerialGC`,
`-Xbatch`, `TieredStopAtLevel=1` — all tried, floor bottoms out ~15,000 in 121
chunks and never reaches zero. Structural reason: a chunk reaching FULL forces
its neighbours to FEATURES, so every forceload decorates a small batch whose
internal order is the scheduler's.

**KILLED — do not re-run: "more twin pairs averages the floor down."** It
cannot. `floor_N` is the size of the set of positions vanilla fails to
reproduce, so it only grows: overworld 35,531 → 73,820, nether 317,725 →
668,532 at N=6. floor/residual therefore gets *worse* with N and **no N makes
the nether quotable**. What an ensemble does buy is a sharper residual —
overworld 43,041 → **37,471** (converged, last reference moved it 1.1%),
nether 254,799 → **151,434** (NOT converged, still moving 4.7%).

**Our own generator is reproducible; nothing needed fixing.** Overworld r=16:
three runs at 12 workers plus one at `RUSTMC_WORKERS=1`, all byte-identical, and
the concurrency is real (2.9x cpu/wall at W=24). **Caveat that must travel:**

### RULE 7 PAID OUT AGAIN, AND THE INSTRUMENT NOW REFUSES THE TRAP

The first run of that measurement reported **zero mismatches for every one of
the eight orders**, including `reverse`, which gives 59,172 on window one.
That is not a result, it is a broken run: `ISECT_TWIN=oracle-work/van-s2-c62`
existed on the laptop and had never been copied to the Threadripper.
`region-differ` exited non-zero, printed nothing, and
`ci/decorate-order-intersect.sh` piped it straight into `grep` with
`2>/dev/null` — so the exit status was the grep's and the silence read as a
clean world.

Fixed in the script, not in a habit: the twin directory is checked before
anything is generated, the differ's output goes to a file so its exit status
survives, and an order whose diff prints no `DIFF` line aborts the run rather
than contributing a zero to the intersection.

**If a measurement clears every candidate, it has cleared the measurement
too.** Sixteen payouts before this one, and the giveaway here was free: an
order that produced 59,172 blocks on one window cannot produce 0 on another.

### WHERE IT IS: TERRAIN, AND UPSTREAM OF DECORATION

Both directions being nearly equal says *misplaced*, not *miscoloured*, and a
column confirms it. At (915, z=1028):

```text
  y   vanilla      ours
  67  air          soul_sand
  ..
  64  air          soul_sand
  63  soul_sand    soul_sand
  62  soul_sand    air
  ..
  58  soul_sand    air
  57  air          air
```

A six-block slab of soul sand with air above **and** below, sitting about five
blocks higher in ours. The soul sand valley's surface rules convert a thin
sliver of terrain entirely, so a terrain difference shows up as
`soul_sand <-> air` and never as `netherrack <-> air`. Across 496 columns that
have both directions the offset is not a constant: it spreads y+2..y+17 with a
mode at 8. **It follows the terrain.**

Split by whether the solid/air **mask** disagrees or only the material, over
chunks (57,64)..(63,79) — 448 sections, 1,835,008 blocks, a quarter of the
window:

```text
  identical               1,828,094
  solid/air MASK differs      4,459     65% — the shape itself
  material only differs       2,455
```

And then the decisive one. `RUSTMC_THROUGH=noise|surface|carvers` stops our
pipeline early, so the same mask comparison can be run against our own
partial worlds:

```text

  vanilla-full  vs  ours-CARVERS    mask differs   4,544
  ours-CARVERS  vs  ours-FULL       mask differs      85
```

**Decoration moves the nether's solid/air mask by 85 blocks and the
disagreement is 4,459.** The defect is entirely upstream of decoration. Every
feature-level hypothesis — basalt deltas, blobs, the delta feature — is
excluded by that line, and `basalt -> air` being 1,515 is a *consequence* of
the terrain moving, not a feature bug.

### THE DENSITY FUNCTION IS BIT-EXACT — AND THAT WITHDRAWS THE LINE ABOVE IT

This section said "the nether defect is in the noise stage" and named a column
as proof. **The measurement it asked for has now been taken and it says the
opposite.** Recorded rather than quietly edited, because the wrong conclusion
was published in a commit message and the docs outrank it.

`ci/nether-density-probe.sh` and `worldgen-dump nether-density` are the two
halves of the same question — vanilla's nether `finalDensity` up a column and
ours, printed identically, raw bits included. At seed 20260722, column
(915,1028), y 55..70:

```text
  every y, both sides:   value and bits IDENTICAL
  y=60   -1.3726560811270222E-4   bf21fdde986d64cf
  y=63    0.006669046966466975    3f7b5100a9dd0901
  y=64    0.006138731536192786    3f7924ed32fd6d58
```

and all **eight lattice corners** of the disputed cell — x 912/916, z
1028/1032, y 56/64 — agree bit for bit as well.

**So the whole density path is exact**: `old_blended_noise` at the
nether-only `y_scale 0.375` / `y_factor 60`, the slide, the squeeze, and the
legacy un-forked `LegacyRandomSource(seed)` seeding. That was the leading
suspect and it is cleared. Do not re-open it.

### WHAT THE COLUMN ACTUALLY SHOWS, RE-READ

Our noise-stage world has solid at 63..67 in that column, and the true corner
values interpolate to a zero crossing at y≈62.5 — so **our fill is doing the
right thing with the right numbers.** Vanilla's *finished* world has solid at
58..63, where the density is negative at 58..62 and positive at 64. Vanilla's
blocks there therefore do not come from its fill either.

The earlier argument — "decoration moves the mask by 85, so the defect is
upstream" — has a hole, and it is worth naming because it is the kind that
survives being read: **85 is how much OUR decoration moves OUR mask.** It
bounds nothing about vanilla's. If vanilla's nether decoration writes
thousands of blocks and ours writes almost none, our side is quiet for the
wrong reason and the comparison reads as "not decoration".

### THE FILL IS EXACT — TWO CHUNKS, 65,536 BLOCKS, ZERO

`ci/nether-fill-probe.sh` is the harness this section asked for, and it was
built and run **before** any nether feature was touched, which was the whole
point of asking for it in that order.

It runs vanilla's own fill: a real `NoiseChunk` built through the public
constructor with vanilla's own `createFluidPicker` and the package-private
`BeardifierMarker.INSTANCE` (both by `setAccessible`, as `GoldenDump` already
does for `Marker`), driven by the loop transcribed out of
`NoiseBasedChunkGenerator.doFill`'s bytecode. `--chunk` prints every non-air
block of the whole chunk, so the comparison is a chunk and not a column.

Against our own `RUSTMC_THROUGH=noise` world at seed 20260722:

```text
  chunk (57,64)   32,768 blocks   14,382 non-air   mismatches 0
  chunk (58,68)   32,768 blocks   23,038 non-air   mismatches 0
```

(58,68) is the **worst chunk in the finished nether diff** — 1,243 mismatched
blocks there — and its fill is byte-identical. So the 24,220 is entirely
downstream of the fill: surface, carvers, features and structures. **The
terrain question is closed. Do not re-open the noise stage, the density
function, the interpolation lattice or the legacy seeding without new
evidence; all four are now measured, not argued.**

The column that started this — (915,1028), where our world has the slab at
63..67 and vanilla's finished world has soul sand at 58..63 — reads correctly
now. Vanilla's *fill* puts netherrack at 63..67 there too, exactly as ours
does. The soul sand at 58..62 in vanilla's finished world is placed by
something after the fill, and finding what places it is the nether's next
question rather than its terrain.

### `basalt_pillar` IS FIXED AND ENABLED — ORACLE §22 FOR THE FOURTH TIME

The 3,437 refusals were never a missing predicate. The feature was ported and
wired, and its parse arm was made unreachable because enabling it moved this
window from 24,245 to **72,684** — a regression of 48,439 blocks. It was put on
`KNOWN_UNPORTED` and left there for two turns.

**The regression was a second defect.** `BasaltPillarFeature.place`, offsets
16-41:

```text
  16: isEmptyBlock(pos)          23: ifeq 39   -> not empty, return false
  26: isEmptyBlock(pos.above())  36: ifeq 41   -> NOT empty, carry on
  39: iconst_0; ireturn                        -> above IS empty, refuse
```

Reaching `return false` at 39 needs `isEmptyBlock(above)` to be **true**. So
the rule is *the origin is air and the block above it is solid* — a pillar
hangs from a ceiling. The port asked for two empty blocks, so a pillar could
start anywhere with headroom, high in a cavern, and the drop loop ran until it
hit something.

The arithmetic said so before the bytecode did, and the sequence is worth
keeping because it is how to work one of these:

```text
  enable it              24,220 -> 72,659   (reproduced; was 72,684)
  where is the damage?   basalt-involved 51,348   other 21,311
  other went DOWN        24,220 -> 21,311, so the draw stream is FINE —
                         this is not a desync, it is the feature itself
  how much basalt?       vanilla 24,333   ours 70,057   ours-without 21,942
  what shape?            17,746 columns, median 1, max 84, ~360 pillars
                         at ~134 blocks each against vanilla's ~7
```

A feature whose every instance is ten times too long is not a neighbourhood
problem. **`other` going down was the decisive line**: it ruled out the
draw-stream desync that a 3x regression normally means, and it did so before
a single byte of bytecode was read.

```text
  nether residual   24,220 -> 22,014      with the pillar ENABLED
  basalt            ours 24,433   vanilla 24,333   (the bug gave 70,057)
```

Re-decomposed after the fix, and it is still almost entirely order-invariant:

```text
  default 22014  diag 22014  spawn 22367  zx 22379  spiral 22455
  spiral_in 29147  zx_rev 26906  reverse 29501  zx_zrev 30077
  intersection  22014 -> 22014 -> 22014 -> 22001, and 22001 thereafter
```

`minecraft:basalt_pillar` is off `KNOWN_UNPORTED`. **An entry earned by a
regression is a hypothesis, not a verdict**, and that list is the wrong place
to keep one — `root_system` is the only member now, and it is a different kind
of entry: no implementation at all.
